A town named for a tree.

The municipal heritage page records an Iba that was once abundant here, became a symbol of the town, and is now locally rare. Its fruit is sharply sour and belongs in the local kitchen.

In the kitchen
Souring agent for fish, and the base for vinegar, wine, and sweets soaked in limewater.
In the landscape
Few old trees remain. The page notes that the Iba is not found in neighbouring towns.
In the barangays
A municipal planting programme has reached every barangay, with Iba-lik ang Kasaysayan as its local heritage project.

Read the full Iba profile →

Five neighbours.

Ibaan sits at 13°49′03″N 121°07′59″E, about 13 kilometres from Batangas City. Its 68.99 square kilometres make up 2.21% of the province.

  • San Jose northwest
  • Lipa City northeast
  • Rosario east
  • Taysan southeast
  • Batangas City southwest
